name: MVP Job 01 · Make a fitted notebook tray
description: Eight job words for make a fitted notebook tray. Practice the meanings, then point to, sketch, calculate, or explain an example in your project. Knowledge target: Phase 1 job vocabulary. Practical skills are assessed in the job itself.

terms.definition: A measured or specified size, such as length, width, or height.
terms.example: Label the tray's base length, base width, and wall height as separate dimensions.

terms.definition: A named amount used to express a measurement, such as an inch, foot, or second.
terms.example: Write 5 1/2 in, not just 5 1/2, so your partner knows which unit to use.

terms.definition: A number that expresses parts of a whole; the denominator names the equal parts and the numerator counts them.
terms.example: A clearance of 1/8 in on each side adds 2/8 in, or 1/4 in, to a notebook dimension.

terms.definition: The smallest marked step a measuring tool can show; it does not guarantee the measurement is accurate.
terms.example: A tape with sixteenth-inch marks has a marked resolution of 1/16 in; check alignment before trusting the reading.

terms.definition: The space intentionally left between a part and another surface so the part can fit or move.
terms.example: Add two 1/8-in clearances to the notebook width to find the tray's inside base width.

terms.definition: The starting piece of material before it is folded or shaped into the finished part.
terms.example: For the model tray, a 5 3/4-in base plus two 3/4-in walls needs a 7 1/4-in blank length.

terms.definition: Written directions that identify the job, dimensions, materials, and requirements for the person doing the work.
terms.example: Your partner builds the tray from a work order showing base size, blank size, wall height, and units.

terms.definition: Not to scale: a drawing whose written dimensions must be used because its drawn lengths are not proportional to the real sizes.
terms.example: Mark your notebook sketch NTS and write the dimensions the builder must follow.

name: MVP Job 02 · Survey one school zone
description: Eight job words for survey one school zone. Practice the meanings, then point to, sketch, calculate, or explain an example in your project. Knowledge target: Phase 1 job vocabulary. Practical skills are assessed in the job itself.

terms.definition: A chosen reference point, line, or surface from which measurements are taken.
terms.example: Name corner A as the datum and locate three school-zone features from it.

terms.definition: A recorded set of observations and measurements describing a site or work area.
terms.example: Your survey includes a sketch, checked dimensions, and the positions of three features.

terms.definition: A point that marks the beginning or end of a measured distance.
terms.example: Record whether the tape ends at a desk edge or its center; those endpoints give different lengths.

terms.definition: A chain of labeled distances between successive features on a drawing.
terms.example: Add three consecutive wall segments and compare their sum with the overall wall measurement.

terms.definition: A difference between values or records that are expected to agree.
terms.example: If the segment sum is 75 in but the direct measurement is 74 3/4 in, investigate the 1/4-in discrepancy.

terms.definition: Expressing the same quantity in another unit without changing its size.
terms.example: Convert 3 ft 4 in to 40 in before adding it to another length in inches.

terms.definition: The full distance between the outside endpoints of an object or layout.
terms.example: Measure the zone from its first boundary to its last boundary as one overall dimension.

terms.definition: An identified change to a drawing, plan, or product that replaces an earlier version.
terms.example: After checking an unclear endpoint, date the drawing and label the corrected version revision B.

name: MVP Job 03 · Lay out a work area
description: Eight job words for lay out a work area. Practice the meanings, then point to, sketch, calculate, or explain an example in your project. Knowledge target: Phase 1 job vocabulary. Practical skills are assessed in the job itself.

terms.definition: The planned or marked positions of parts, edges, and reference lines before making or placing something.
terms.example: Lay out the work area's boundaries and fixture locations before placing the paper equipment.

terms.definition: A number that locates a point relative to a stated origin and direction; a plan often needs two coordinates.
terms.example: In the 36 × 48 in model, the center is 18 in in one direction and 24 in in the other from the datum.

terms.definition: A reference line through the middle of a feature, used to locate or align it.
terms.example: Mark the work area's middle line so both fixture points share one centerline.

terms.definition: A stated distance and direction from a reference line or point to a feature.
terms.example: Locate a fixture 12 in inward from the short end and state the reference edge.

terms.definition: Meeting at a right angle of 90 degrees.
terms.example: The two directions used for the rectangular work-area coordinates meet at 90 degrees.

terms.definition: A line segment joining two corners of a shape that are not next to each other.
terms.example: Measure from one corner to the opposite corner, then check the other diagonal.

terms.definition: For a right triangle, the square of the longest side equals the sum of the squares of the other two sides: c² = a² + b².
terms.example: For the 36 × 48 in rectangle, the ideal diagonal is √(36² + 48²) = 60 in.

terms.definition: Having the intended right angles; a rectangular layout must be checked against its side lengths and geometry.
terms.example: Check side lengths and corner geometry before calling the work-area layout square; one correct diagonal is insufficient.

name: MVP Job 04 · Estimate a display surface
description: Eight job words for estimate a display surface. Practice the meanings, then point to, sketch, calculate, or explain an example in your project. Knowledge target: Phase 1 job vocabulary. Practical skills are assessed in the job itself.

terms.definition: The amount of a flat surface, measured in square units; a rectangle has area length × width.
terms.example: The model 4 × 6 ft display has 24 ft² of surface to cover.

terms.definition: The total distance around the boundary of a flat shape.
terms.example: The same display needs 2 × 4 + 2 × 6 = 20 ft of border before cutting allowances.

terms.definition: An area unit equal to a square one unit long and one unit wide, such as in² or ft².
terms.example: Panel coverage is recorded in ft²; border length is recorded in ft.

terms.definition: The count or measured amount of an item needed or purchased.
terms.example: A feasible layout uses four 2 × 3 ft panels to cover the model display.

terms.definition: The price for one stated unit, such as one sheet or one foot of material.
terms.example: At the fictional unit price of $4 per panel, each additional panel adds $4.

terms.definition: The total for one item or group before other items, taxes, or fees are added.
terms.example: Four panels at $4 each give a panel subtotal of $16 before adding the border.

terms.definition: A list of the finished pieces to make, with each piece's size and quantity.
terms.example: List two 6-ft border pieces and two 4-ft border pieces before deciding how much stock to buy.

terms.definition: Material that cannot be used in the planned job, such as cutting loss or unusable scraps.
terms.example: Keep usable border offcuts separate from material that cannot serve this display job.

name: MVP Job 05 · Handle a change order
description: Eight job words for handle a change order. Practice the meanings, then point to, sketch, calculate, or explain an example in your project. Knowledge target: Phase 1 job vocabulary. Practical skills are assessed in the job itself.

terms.definition: A documented change to the agreed job requirements, including any effects on dimensions, cost, or time.
terms.example: The owner requests an extra 1/8 in of clearance on every side; record that change before rebuilding.

terms.definition: An identified change to a drawing, plan, or product that replaces an earlier version.
terms.example: Highlight the changed tray dimensions on revision B while retaining the unchanged wall height.

terms.definition: An amount deliberately included for a stated purpose, such as overlap, cutting loss, or material thickness.
terms.example: Include both 3/4-in wall allowances when recalculating each blank dimension.

terms.definition: The space intentionally left between a part and another surface so the part can fit or move.
terms.example: Increasing the gap by 1/8 in on both sides increases the base dimension by 1/4 in.

terms.definition: A limit the design must satisfy, such as available space, materials, cost, or time.
terms.example: The revised blank must fit the available paper or have a planned joined-sheet construction.

terms.definition: A distance between the inner faces of a part or opening.
terms.example: The model's inside base grows from 5 3/4 × 3 3/4 in to 6 × 4 in.

terms.definition: A distance between the outer faces of a part or assembly.
terms.example: The finished tray's outside size includes its wall material; do not confuse it with the flat blank size.

terms.definition: To check a claim, value, or condition against a measurement, calculation, or other evidence.
terms.example: Check the new blank dimensions and test the revised fit before accepting the change.

name: MVP Job 06 · Make a replacement template
description: Eight job words for make a replacement template. Practice the meanings, then point to, sketch, calculate, or explain an example in your project. Knowledge target: Phase 1 job vocabulary. Practical skills are assessed in the job itself.

terms.definition: A pattern used to transfer a shape or feature locations to another piece of material.
terms.example: Make a paper pattern another student can use to reproduce the replacement liner.

terms.definition: A space set back within a surface or boundary that another part may fit into.
terms.example: Measure the inside edges of the space where the replacement liner must sit.

terms.definition: The space intentionally left between a part and another surface so the part can fit or move.
terms.example: For a 12-in recess with a 1/8-in gap at both edges, make the liner 11 3/4 in wide.

terms.definition: A chosen reference point, line, or surface from which measurements are taken.
terms.example: Locate the liner's cutout from the same reference corner used in the survey.

terms.definition: An opening or removed section made to clear a feature or allow access.
terms.example: Remove only the section needed to clear a measured feature in the recess.

terms.definition: Making a part from material by operations such as marking, cutting, folding, and joining.
terms.example: Mark, cut, and check the paper liner using the dimensions on your work order.

terms.definition: The allowed variation from a specified dimension or value.
terms.example: State the permitted dimensional variation before deciding whether the replacement matches the specification.

terms.definition: How well a part matches its intended space and required clearance.
terms.example: Place the template in the recess and check the intended gap along every edge.

name: MVP Job 07 · Space five mounting centers
description: Eight job words for space five mounting centers. Practice the meanings, then point to, sketch, calculate, or explain an example in your project. Knowledge target: Phase 2 job vocabulary. Practical skills are assessed in the job itself.

terms.definition: A reference line through the middle of a feature, used to locate or align it.
terms.example: Mark each of the five mounting positions at its center, not at the edge of a hypothetical fastener.

terms.definition: The distance from an end of a layout to the first or last specified feature.
terms.example: Leave 3 in from each end of the 30-in strip to the first and last mounting centers.

terms.definition: The distance or time between consecutive marks, points, or events.
terms.example: Five centers create four intervals between the first center and the last.

terms.definition: Placing successive reference points the same distance apart.
terms.example: The usable 24-in distance divided into four intervals gives 6-in spacing.

terms.definition: A number that locates a point relative to a stated origin and direction; a plan often needs two coordinates.
terms.example: Record the centers as 3, 9, 15, 21, and 27 in from the datum.

terms.definition: A chosen reference point, line, or surface from which measurements are taken.
terms.example: Take every mounting coordinate from the same starting end of the strip.

terms.definition: The allowed variation from a specified dimension or value.
terms.example: Check the mounting marks against the classroom requirement of ±1/8 in.

terms.definition: Error that adds up across a sequence of measurements or layout steps.
terms.example: Repeatedly measuring from the last mark can carry earlier mistakes forward; check every mark from the datum.

name: MVP Job 08 · Draw a plan to scale
description: Eight job words for draw a plan to scale. Practice the meanings, then point to, sketch, calculate, or explain an example in your project. Knowledge target: Phase 2 job vocabulary. Practical skills are assessed in the job itself.

terms.definition: The stated relationship between a drawing length and the actual length it represents.
terms.example: At 1 in = 2 ft, a 12-ft wall is drawn 6 in long.

terms.definition: The multiplier between corresponding lengths when both lengths use the same unit.
terms.example: Because 2 ft = 24 in, the drawing-to-actual scale factor is 1/24.

terms.definition: A drawing showing a space or object as viewed from directly above.
terms.example: Show the zone boundaries and equipment as seen from above.

terms.definition: The area or outline an object occupies when viewed from above.
terms.example: A 4 × 2 ft desk has a 2 × 1 in paper footprint at the chosen scale.

terms.definition: An equality between two ratios, used to compare corresponding quantities.
terms.example: The proportion 1 drawing inch / 2 actual feet = 3 drawing inches / 6 actual feet keeps the scale consistent.

terms.definition: The full-size measurement of the real object or space, rather than its drawing size.
terms.example: Label the real desk width as 2 ft even though its paper width is only 1 in.

terms.definition: A measured or specified size, such as length, width, or height.
terms.example: Write the actual length and width next to each paper equipment piece.

terms.definition: The routes people use to move through a space.
terms.example: Use the plan to keep the teacher-defined model walking route clear of equipment footprints.

name: MVP Job 09 · Plan cuts from stock
description: Eight job words for plan cuts from stock. Practice the meanings, then point to, sketch, calculate, or explain an example in your project. Knowledge target: Phase 2 job vocabulary. Practical skills are assessed in the job itself.

terms.definition: Material in the starting size available for making parts.
terms.example: Start the cutting plan with one 48-in stock strip.

terms.definition: The required length of a completed part after cutting and other operations.
terms.example: Each completed model part must be 11 3/4 in long, excluding the cutting loss.

terms.definition: The width of material removed by a cutting tool, which must be included when planning cuts.
terms.example: Represent each separating cut with a 1/8-in strip of lost material in the paper plan.

terms.definition: A list of the finished pieces to make, with each piece's size and quantity.
terms.example: The job's cut list calls for four parts, each 11 3/4 in long.

terms.definition: A piece left after cutting that may still be usable for another part.
terms.example: After four parts and four cuts, a 1/2-in piece of stock remains; decide whether it is useful.

terms.definition: Material removed by the cuts, separate from usable pieces and remaining offcuts.
terms.example: Four cuts at 1/8 in each remove 1/2 in of stock in the model.

terms.definition: A way to write numbers using place values based on powers of ten, including positions after a decimal point.
terms.example: Write 11 3/4 in as 11.75 in to check the stock calculation using decimals.

terms.definition: A number that expresses parts of a whole; the denominator names the equal parts and the numerator counts them.
terms.example: Four 11 3/4-in parts total 47 in before adding the four cutting allowances.

name: MVP Job 10 · Compare two material quotes
description: Eight job words for compare two material quotes. Practice the meanings, then point to, sketch, calculate, or explain an example in your project. Knowledge target: Phase 2 job vocabulary. Practical skills are assessed in the job itself.

terms.definition: A stated price offer for a described quantity and scope of goods or work.
terms.example: Write two offers that state panel size, quantity, price, and the costs excluded from the comparison.

terms.definition: The price for one stated unit, such as one sheet or one foot of material.
terms.example: Supplier A's fictional $7 per panel is a unit price; panel sizes must also be compared.

terms.definition: The count or measured amount of an item needed or purchased.
terms.example: A feasible layout needs six panels from A or four from B in the supplied model.

terms.definition: The total for one item or group before other items, taxes, or fees are added.
terms.example: Six panels at $7 produce a $42 material subtotal for option A.

terms.definition: The sum of all included costs, with any exclusions stated.
terms.example: The classroom comparison is $42 versus $44, excluding tax, delivery, and labor.

terms.definition: The area remaining after specified openings or excluded areas are subtracted from the gross area.
terms.example: With no excluded openings, the 6 × 8 ft job needs 48 ft² of coverage.

terms.definition: Material that cannot be used in the planned job, such as cutting loss or unusable scraps.
terms.example: Calculate purchased area minus covered area, then distinguish unusable scraps from reusable offcuts.

terms.definition: A condition treated as true for planning or calculation that must be stated and checked when possible.
terms.example: State the model's assumption that the panel sizes tile the surface without cutting loss.

name: MVP Job 11 · Inspect a layout discrepancy
description: Eight job words for inspect a layout discrepancy. Practice the meanings, then point to, sketch, calculate, or explain an example in your project. Knowledge target: Phase 2 job vocabulary. Practical skills are assessed in the job itself.

terms.definition: A written requirement describing what a part, system, or job must be like.
terms.example: The inspected length is specified as 40 in with a classroom tolerance of ±1/4 in.

terms.definition: A number with a unit obtained from a stated measurement method.
terms.example: Record the actual tape reading of 40 3/8 in before judging whether it passes.

terms.definition: A subtraction result that keeps its positive or negative sign; measured minus specified shows the direction of a dimensional error.
terms.example: Measured minus specified is 40 3/8 − 40 = +3/8 in, showing the layout is too long.

terms.definition: The size of the difference between two values without a positive or negative direction.
terms.example: The magnitude of a −1/8-in signed difference is 1/8 in.

terms.definition: The allowed variation from a specified dimension or value.
terms.example: The permitted variation is 1/4 in shorter or longer than the specified 40 in.

terms.definition: The interval of values permitted by the stated limits or tolerance.
terms.example: The acceptable interval is 39 3/4 to 40 1/4 in, including the endpoints.

terms.definition: A difference between values or records that are expected to agree.
terms.example: Compare all inspection readings to identify which location or dimension disagrees with the plan.

terms.definition: Work done again or corrected because the result did not meet a requirement.
terms.example: Correct the dimension that failed, then measure again before marking it accepted.

name: MVP Job 12 · Deliver a buildable job package
description: Eight job words for deliver a buildable job package. Practice the meanings, then point to, sketch, calculate, or explain an example in your project. Knowledge target: Phase 2 job vocabulary. Practical skills are assessed in the job itself.

terms.definition: Written directions that identify the job, dimensions, materials, and requirements for the person doing the work.
terms.example: Give another group the drawings, material requirements, and checks needed to make the divider model.

terms.definition: A drawing showing a space or object as viewed from directly above.
terms.example: Show the two divider centerlines at 6 and 12 in in the 18-in zero-thickness model.

terms.definition: A drawing looking straight at a vertical face, showing heights and vertical relationships.
terms.example: Show the selected divider height in a view of its vertical face.

terms.definition: An itemized list of materials and components, including sizes and quantities needed for an assembly.
terms.example: List paper sheets and tape segments with their sizes, quantities, and simulated prices.

terms.definition: A list of the finished pieces to make, with each piece's size and quantity.
terms.example: List each divider and base piece separately so a builder knows what to cut.

terms.definition: An amount deliberately included for a stated purpose, such as overlap, cutting loss, or material thickness.
terms.example: State that real divider thickness reduces the clear bay width even when centerlines stay 6 in apart.

terms.definition: An identified change to a drawing, plan, or product that replaces an earlier version.
terms.example: Make sure the estimate and both drawings refer to the same version of the divider design.

terms.definition: A measurable requirement or stated test used to decide whether the work meets the job's needs.
terms.example: One criterion is that a partner can locate both divider centers from your drawing without guessing.

name: MVP Job 13 · Fold a stronger beam
description: Eight job words for fold a stronger beam. Practice the meanings, then point to, sketch, calculate, or explain an example in your project. Knowledge target: Phase 3 job vocabulary. Practical skills are assessed in the job itself.

terms.definition: A structural member that carries loads across a span mainly by resisting bending.
terms.example: The paper member bridges two supports and carries the small test objects.

terms.definition: The shape exposed by an imaginary cut across an object, such as the end shape of a folded beam.
terms.example: Compare the flat paper's end shape with the folded beam's end shape.

terms.definition: An external force acting on a structure or part, such as the weight of an object placed on it.
terms.example: Identical erasers apply loads through their weight; an eraser count is not a measured force in newtons.

terms.definition: A part or contact that holds a structure and transfers forces from it to another part or surface.
terms.example: Keep the two supporting surfaces in the same positions for both beam shapes.

terms.definition: How strongly a structure resists deformation under load; it is different from the load it can withstand before failure.
terms.example: Compare bending under the same load to investigate how the fold changes resistance to deformation.

terms.definition: The greatest load or demand that meets a stated performance limit under specified conditions.
terms.example: Record the count at the agreed test limit for each beam; state the limit used.

terms.definition: A comparison of two quantities by division, with units and order stated.
terms.example: A folded beam reaching 8 erasers versus 2 for the flat beam has a capacity-count ratio of 4 to 1 in that test.

terms.definition: A condition deliberately kept the same to make a comparison fair.
terms.example: Use the same paper allowance, support spacing, and loading method when comparing shapes.

name: MVP Job 14 · Test the effect of span
description: Eight job words for test the effect of span. Practice the meanings, then point to, sketch, calculate, or explain an example in your project. Knowledge target: Phase 3 job vocabulary. Practical skills are assessed in the job itself.

terms.definition: The distance between supports, with the measurement endpoints stated as faces or centerlines.
terms.example: Change the stated distance between the beam supports while keeping the beam shape the same.

terms.definition: The change in a part's position caused by loading, measured from its unloaded position.
terms.example: A midspan height changing from 2 in to 1 3/4 in gives 1/4 in of downward deflection.

terms.definition: The condition deliberately changed in an investigation.
terms.example: Support spacing is the condition you deliberately change in this test.

terms.definition: The response measured to see the effect of a changed condition.
terms.example: Midspan deflection is the response you measure at each span.

terms.definition: A condition deliberately kept the same to make a comparison fair.
terms.example: Keep the load, paper, beam shape, and load location the same across span comparisons.

terms.definition: One run of a test using a recorded set of conditions.
terms.example: Record each run and identify whether it used a fresh specimen or a previously loaded one.

terms.definition: A display that locates data using labeled axes so relationships can be examined.
terms.example: Put span in inches on the horizontal axis and deflection in inches on the vertical axis.

terms.definition: The general pattern in a set of results, which may include variation.
terms.example: Describe the span–deflection pattern shown by your results without hiding readings that vary.

name: MVP Job 15 · Brace a frame
description: Eight job words for brace a frame. Practice the meanings, then point to, sketch, calculate, or explain an example in your project. Knowledge target: Phase 3 job vocabulary. Practical skills are assessed in the job itself.

terms.definition: A member added to reduce unwanted movement or deformation of a structure.
terms.example: Add a diagonal paper member to reduce the frame's sideways distortion.

terms.definition: A line segment joining two corners of a shape that are not next to each other.
terms.example: The brace runs between opposite corner reference points of the frame.

terms.definition: Arranging members into triangles to resist changes of shape when the members and connections hold their lengths.
terms.example: The diagonal divides the rectangular frame into triangles when its joints hold.

terms.definition: A sideways distortion that changes the angles of a frame, such as a rectangle leaning into a parallelogram.
terms.example: Observe how the unbraced rectangular frame changes into a slanted shape under sideways movement.

terms.definition: The length or area where one part extends over another to make a connection.
terms.example: Add the measured attachment length at both ends beyond the corner-to-corner brace distance.

terms.definition: The place and method by which two or more parts are connected.
terms.example: Inspect the taped brace connections because a loose joint can let the frame move.

terms.definition: For a right triangle, the square of the longest side equals the sum of the squares of the other two sides: c² = a² + b².
terms.example: A 6 × 8 in right-angle frame has a 10-in corner-to-corner distance before attachment allowances.

terms.definition: A change in position with its direction stated.
terms.example: Apply the same initial sideways displacement when comparing the braced and unbraced frames.

name: MVP Job 16 · Place the supports
description: Eight job words for place the supports. Practice the meanings, then point to, sketch, calculate, or explain an example in your project. Knowledge target: Phase 3 job vocabulary. Practical skills are assessed in the job itself.

terms.definition: A part or contact that holds a structure and transfers forces from it to another part or surface.
terms.example: Place five supports under the paper member at the planned positions.

terms.definition: The distance between supports, with the measurement endpoints stated as faces or centerlines.
terms.example: The 0-to-24-in model has four 6-in spans between support centerlines.

terms.definition: A reference line through the middle of a feature, used to locate or align it.
terms.example: Locate each support by its middle rather than switching between edges and centers.

terms.definition: The distance or time between consecutive marks, points, or events.
terms.example: Divide 24 in by four intervals, not by the five support points.

terms.definition: The route by which forces pass through connected parts and supports.
terms.example: Draw arrows showing how the applied load passes through the member to the supports.

terms.definition: A force a support exerts on the structure it holds.
terms.example: A support pushes back on the loaded member; the forces need not be equal at every support.

terms.definition: The length of a member between locations that actually provide the relevant support.
terms.example: Removing a support can increase the length that must bridge without support.

terms.definition: A number that locates a point relative to a stated origin and direction; a plan often needs two coordinates.
terms.example: Label support positions 0, 6, 12, 18, and 24 in from one datum.

name: MVP Job 17 · Spread the bearing load
description: Eight job words for spread the bearing load. Practice the meanings, then point to, sketch, calculate, or explain an example in your project. Knowledge target: Phase 3 job vocabulary. Practical skills are assessed in the job itself.

terms.definition: The contact area over which one part transfers a compressive force to another.
terms.example: Calculate the area of each paper foot where it touches the pad.

terms.definition: Normal force per contact area; average pressure = force ÷ area.
terms.example: In the supplied model, 12 N on 2 cm² gives an average pressure of 6 N/cm².

terms.definition: A push or pull that can change motion or deform an object.
terms.example: Keep the same applied load when comparing the effects of different foot areas.

terms.definition: The SI unit of force, written N.
terms.example: Use N only for a supplied or measured force; do not relabel an unknown object count as newtons.

terms.definition: A loading action that pushes parts of a material toward one another.
terms.example: The support foot pushes into the pad and compresses it.

terms.definition: A change in an object's shape or size caused by a load or other action.
terms.example: Record the pad's indentation or change in shape as an observation, not as a direct pressure reading.

terms.definition: A relationship in which one quantity decreases as another increases; for constant force, pressure varies as 1 ÷ area.
terms.example: At a fixed 12 N, increasing contact area from 2 to 6 cm² reduces average pressure from 6 to 2 N/cm².

terms.definition: An area unit equal to a square one unit long and one unit wide, such as in² or ft².
terms.example: A 2 cm by 3 cm foot has a bearing area of 6 cm².

name: MVP Job 18 · Establish a level reference
description: Eight job words for establish a level reference. Practice the meanings, then point to, sketch, calculate, or explain an example in your project. Knowledge target: Phase 4 job vocabulary. Practical skills are assessed in the job itself.

terms.definition: Horizontal: perpendicular to the local direction of gravity.
terms.example: Verify the reference is horizontal before comparing the two vertical drops.

terms.definition: The vertical position of a point relative to a chosen reference level.
terms.example: Compare the points' vertical positions relative to the same checked reference.

terms.definition: A downward distance measured vertically from a stated reference.
terms.example: A point 3 1/4 in below the line has a greater drop than a point 2 in below it.

terms.definition: A fixed reference point with an established elevation used to compare other elevations.
terms.example: Use a fixed point on the checked level reference as the project's elevation reference.

terms.definition: Along a level direction, perpendicular to local vertical.
terms.example: The reference line must be horizontal; a straight but sloping line is unsuitable.

terms.definition: Vertical: aligned with the local direction of gravity.
terms.example: Measure each drop vertically rather than along a tilted tape.

terms.definition: A marked or established line used as the basis for locating or measuring other features.
terms.example: Keep the same line for both readings so the difference has a valid basis.

terms.definition: The size of the difference between two values without a positive or negative direction.
terms.example: The two supplied drops differ by 1 1/4 in; also name which point is lower.

name: MVP Job 19 · Lay out a sloping route
description: Eight job words for lay out a sloping route. Practice the meanings, then point to, sketch, calculate, or explain an example in your project. Knowledge target: Phase 4 job vocabulary. Practical skills are assessed in the job itself.

terms.definition: Vertical rise or fall divided by horizontal run, with the direction and units stated.
terms.example: The model route falls 1/4 in for each foot of horizontal run.

terms.definition: The horizontal distance used in a slope calculation, rather than the length along the inclined surface.
terms.example: Use 6 ft of horizontal distance, or 72 in, for the slope denominator.

terms.definition: The decrease in elevation from the start of a route to its end.
terms.example: At 1/4 in per foot over 6 ft, total endpoint fall is 1 1/2 in.

terms.definition: Vertical change ÷ horizontal run × 100%, using the same length unit for both distances.
terms.example: The supplied route has 1.5/72 × 100% ≈ 2.08% slope.

terms.definition: The vertical position of a point relative to a chosen reference level.
terms.example: Mark the route's end elevation 1 1/2 in below its start in the supplied model.

terms.definition: A drawing looking straight at a vertical face, showing heights and vertical relationships.
terms.example: Use a side view to show the route's heights as well as its horizontal distance.

terms.definition: The stated relationship between a drawing length and the actual length it represents.
terms.example: If the side view enlarges vertical distances, label both the vertical and horizontal scales.

terms.definition: A local downward bend or low spot below the intended route or shape.
terms.example: Inspect for a local low spot; correct endpoint fall does not rule out a sag along the route.

name: MVP Job 20 · Coordinate a dry service bay
description: Eight job words for coordinate a dry service bay. Practice the meanings, then point to, sketch, calculate, or explain an example in your project. Knowledge target: Phase 4 job vocabulary. Practical skills are assessed in the job itself.

terms.definition: The planned path followed by a service, material, or moving object.
terms.example: Draw the two dry model service paths before constructing their crossing.

terms.definition: A defined space allocated to systems and their supports, clearances, and access.
terms.example: Keep both routes, their thicknesses, and the required gap inside the 6-in-deep model bay.

terms.definition: A location where two routes pass across one another in plan and their vertical separation must be checked.
terms.example: Check the point where the two routes overlap in plan using a matching side view.

terms.definition: The space intentionally left between a part and another surface so the part can fit or move.
terms.example: Include the specified 1/2-in gap between the two model routes.

terms.definition: An accounting of the available vertical depth and all the layers, gaps, and allowances that use it.
terms.example: The 1-in route, 1/2-in gap, and 1 1/2-in route occupy 3 in of depth.

terms.definition: The distance between the two opposite faces of a material layer or part.
terms.example: Include each route's full thickness when locating its top and bottom surfaces.

terms.definition: A drawing showing a space or object as viewed from directly above.
terms.example: Use the overhead view to locate where the routes cross.

terms.definition: Checking that related drawings, dimensions, components, and routes work together without conflict.
terms.example: Make sure the route order and positions agree in the plan, side view, and model.

name: MVP Job 21 · Revise an elevation budget
description: Eight job words for revise an elevation budget. Practice the meanings, then point to, sketch, calculate, or explain an example in your project. Knowledge target: Phase 4 job vocabulary. Practical skills are assessed in the job itself.

terms.definition: An accounting of the available vertical depth and all the layers, gaps, and allowances that use it.
terms.example: Subtract every occupied layer and gap from the supplied 8-in total depth.

terms.definition: The amount left after all stated requirements have been subtracted from an available dimension or budget.
terms.example: The original model has 1 1/2 in left; a 3/4-in thicker finish leaves 3/4 in.

terms.definition: The final surface material, whose thickness can change the space available for a route or part.
terms.example: Show how the changed finish thickness shifts the space available to the routes.

terms.definition: A feature that blocks or limits the proposed route, space, or access.
terms.example: Mark a fixed obstruction so the revised route is checked at the conflict location.

terms.definition: An amount deliberately included for a stated purpose, such as overlap, cutting loss, or material thickness.
terms.example: List support, bend, gap, and route allowances separately so none is omitted or counted twice.

terms.definition: An identified change to a drawing, plan, or product that replaces an earlier version.
terms.example: Update the depth calculation and drawing together after the finish change.

terms.definition: A limit the design must satisfy, such as available space, materials, cost, or time.
terms.example: A positive overall spare depth does not prove that every local crossing fits.

terms.definition: A subtraction result that keeps its positive or negative sign; measured minus specified shows the direction of a dimensional error.
terms.example: Compute revised spare minus original spare to show that available depth decreased by 3/4 in.

name: MVP Job 22 · Measure a flow rate
description: Eight job words for measure a flow rate. Practice the meanings, then point to, sketch, calculate, or explain an example in your project. Knowledge target: Phase 4 job vocabulary. Practical skills are assessed in the job itself.

terms.definition: The volume of fluid passing a point or collected per unit time, such as mL/s.
terms.example: A supplied collection of 240 mL in 12 s has a flow rate of 20 mL/s.

terms.definition: The amount of three-dimensional space occupied or contained, measured in cubic units or units such as milliliters.
terms.example: Record how many milliliters are collected, using the actual reading or a clearly labeled supplied value.

terms.definition: The amount of time between a stated start and finish.
terms.example: Measure from the stated start of collection to its finish.

terms.definition: A rate that stays the same throughout the interval being considered.
terms.example: Predicting 600 mL in 30 s assumes the 20 mL/s rate remains unchanged.

terms.definition: A condition deliberately kept the same to make a comparison fair.
terms.example: Keep the starting reservoir level and timing method comparable when changing the outlet condition.

terms.definition: One run of a test using a recorded set of conditions.
terms.example: Repeat the collection and record each volume and time, instead of keeping only the best result.

terms.definition: The arithmetic average: add the values and divide by the number of values.
terms.example: For equal-duration trials with rates 20, 19, and 21 mL/s, the mean rate is 20 mL/s.

terms.definition: The doubt or range associated with a measurement because tools and methods cannot give an exact value.
terms.example: Identify how reaction time or a hard-to-read volume mark affects confidence in the rate.

name: MVP Job 23 · Estimate a thermal envelope
description: Eight job words for estimate a thermal envelope. Practice the meanings, then point to, sketch, calculate, or explain an example in your project. Knowledge target: Phase 5 job vocabulary. Practical skills are assessed in the job itself.

terms.definition: The parts of an enclosure that separate its inside from outside and affect heat transfer, such as walls, roof, and openings.
terms.example: Identify the model wall and opening that separate the room's inside from its surroundings.

terms.definition: The full area before openings or other excluded areas are subtracted.
terms.example: The supplied wall's full area is 96 ft² before subtracting the opening.

terms.definition: A gap in a surface, such as a window or door space, that must be accounted for in the design.
terms.example: The model has a 12-ft² opening that is excluded from the wall covering estimate.

terms.definition: The area remaining after specified openings or excluded areas are subtracted from the gross area.
terms.example: Subtract 12 ft² from 96 ft² to find 84 ft² of wall covering.

terms.definition: Counting and measuring the material quantities needed from drawings or a surveyed job.
terms.example: Use the wall drawing to list covering areas and the resulting sheet quantities.

terms.definition: A value that the required amount cannot be below, even though practical constraints may require more.
terms.example: Area alone gives a minimum of 11 sheets at 8 ft² each; a feasible cut layout may require more.

terms.definition: To use the next whole purchasable quantity when a calculation gives a partial item.
terms.example: A result of 10.5 sheets requires at least 11 whole sheets for purchase.

terms.definition: The price for one stated unit, such as one sheet or one foot of material.
terms.example: At the fictional $6 per sheet, an 11-sheet material subtotal is $66 before other costs.

name: MVP Job 24 · Compare heat loss
description: Eight job words for compare heat loss. Practice the meanings, then point to, sketch, calculate, or explain an example in your project. Knowledge target: Phase 5 job vocabulary. Practical skills are assessed in the job itself.

terms.definition: A measure of how hot or cold a body is, expressed on a stated scale such as degrees Celsius.
terms.example: Record the cup's temperature in °C at each stated time.

terms.definition: Energy moving from a warmer region to a cooler region because of a temperature difference.
terms.example: The warmer cup transfers energy to its cooler surroundings during the comparison.

terms.definition: Final temperature minus initial temperature; a temperature drop can instead be reported as a positive magnitude.
terms.example: A change from 40°C to 34°C is −6°C, or a temperature drop of 6°C.

terms.definition: The duration between two specified times.
terms.example: Compare both arrangements over the same 10-minute interval.

terms.definition: The total change in a quantity divided by the time interval over which it occurred.
terms.example: A 6°C drop over 10 min is an average cooling magnitude of 0.6°C/min.

terms.definition: A condition deliberately kept the same to make a comparison fair.
terms.example: Keep water amount, starting temperature, and location comparable between cup arrangements.

terms.definition: Material used to slow heat transfer through an assembly.
terms.example: Compare a wrap intended to slow heat transfer with the reference arrangement.

terms.definition: A display that locates data using labeled axes so relationships can be examined.
terms.example: Plot temperature against time and label any supplied dataset as supplied rather than measured by you.

name: MVP Job 25 · Improve a thermal design
description: Eight job words for improve a thermal design. Practice the meanings, then point to, sketch, calculate, or explain an example in your project. Knowledge target: Phase 5 job vocabulary. Practical skills are assessed in the job itself.

terms.definition: A route through which energy can transfer between warmer and cooler parts of a system.
terms.example: Mark possible energy-transfer routes through the sides, lid, and base before changing one.

terms.definition: Heat transfer through a material or contact between materials without bulk motion of the material.
terms.example: A wrap changes the material path through which heat can conduct from the cup toward its surroundings.

terms.definition: Heat transfer between a surface and a moving fluid such as air or water.
terms.example: Air moving near the cup surface can affect heat transfer, so keep the test location comparable.

terms.definition: Material used to slow heat transfer through an assembly.
terms.example: More wrapping uses more material; test whether the revised arrangement reduces cooling under the same conditions.

terms.definition: The decrease divided by the original value, multiplied by 100%.
terms.example: A drop reduced from 8°C to 6°C is 2/8 × 100% = 25% smaller than the original drop.

terms.definition: The original or reference result used for comparison with a changed design or condition.
terms.example: Use the original wrap's result as the comparison point for the revised design.

terms.definition: A condition deliberately kept the same to make a comparison fair.
terms.example: Hold the water volume, initial temperature, location, and test interval the same.

terms.definition: A new test after a change, using stated conditions so the results can be compared.
terms.example: Test the revised wrap under the original conditions and report an inconclusive result honestly if necessary.

name: MVP Job 26 · Build a low-voltage light circuit
description: Eight job words for build a low-voltage light circuit. Practice the meanings, then point to, sketch, calculate, or explain an example in your project. Knowledge target: Phase 5 job vocabulary. Practical skills are assessed in the job itself.

terms.definition: An arrangement of connected electrical components; sustained current requires a complete conducting path through a source and load.
terms.example: Trace a complete path from one source terminal through the switch and lamp to the other terminal.

terms.definition: Electric potential difference: energy transferred per unit charge between two points, measured in volts (V).
terms.example: The supplied resistor example has 6 V across its load.

terms.definition: The rate of flow of electric charge, measured in amperes (A).
terms.example: The model calculation predicts 0.20 A through a 30-Ω resistor at 6 V.

terms.definition: A measure of opposition to current, expressed in ohms (Ω); for a resistor model, R = V ÷ I.
terms.example: The supplied 30-Ω resistor model is not a claim that a real warming lamp has constant resistance.

terms.definition: A component that opens or closes a conducting path in a circuit.
terms.example: Place the switch so opening it interrupts the intended lamp path.

terms.definition: A circuit with a break that prevents sustained current through that path.
terms.example: When the switch opens, the break stops sustained current through the lamp path.

terms.definition: A circuit with a complete conducting path through the source and load.
terms.example: With the switch closed and every connection complete, the source and lamp form a closed path.

terms.definition: The relationship V = I × R for an ohmic component under constant physical conditions such as temperature.
terms.example: Use I = V/R to calculate 6 V / 30 Ω = 0.20 A for the supplied resistor case.

name: MVP Job 27 · Compare series and parallel paths
description: Eight job words for compare series and parallel paths. Practice the meanings, then point to, sketch, calculate, or explain an example in your project. Knowledge target: Phase 5 job vocabulary. Practical skills are assessed in the job itself.

terms.definition: A circuit arrangement with components along one path, so the same current passes through each component.
terms.example: Two supplied 12-Ω resistors in one path have an equivalent resistance of 24 Ω.

terms.definition: A circuit arrangement with branches connected across the same two points, so each branch has the same voltage across it.
terms.example: Two resistor branches connected across the same 6-V source each have 6 V across them.

terms.definition: One path for current between junctions in a circuit.
terms.example: Trace each complete path separately in the parallel drawing.

terms.definition: The current before a set of branches splits, equal to the sum of their currents at that junction.
terms.example: Two supplied parallel branches carrying 0.5 A each draw 1 A in total from the ideal source.

terms.definition: The single resistance that would draw the same total current at the same applied voltage as a resistor network.
terms.example: The two 12-Ω resistors together are 24 Ω in series or 6 Ω in parallel in the ideal model.

terms.definition: Electric potential difference: energy transferred per unit charge between two points, measured in volts (V).
terms.example: Label the voltage across each parallel branch rather than dividing 6 V between those branches.

terms.definition: The rate of flow of electric charge, measured in amperes (A).
terms.example: In the supplied series case, 6 V / 24 Ω = 0.25 A through both resistors.

terms.definition: A connection where circuit paths meet and current can divide or combine.
terms.example: At the parallel split, the incoming current equals the sum of the two outgoing branch currents.

name: MVP Job 28 · Diagnose a circuit fault
description: Eight job words for diagnose a circuit fault. Practice the meanings, then point to, sketch, calculate, or explain an example in your project. Knowledge target: Phase 5 job vocabulary. Practical skills are assessed in the job itself.

terms.definition: A condition that prevents a system from operating as intended.
terms.example: An open switch or a broken lead can prevent the model lamp from operating.

terms.definition: Identifying a problem's cause by following evidence from inspection and tests.
terms.example: Follow a recorded sequence of inspection and approved tests to identify which condition caused the failure.

terms.definition: A testable proposed explanation for an observation or problem.
terms.example: Predict that the lead is disconnected, then name an observation that would support or reject that explanation.

terms.definition: An unbroken conducting path between stated points; continuity alone does not prove that a circuit will operate correctly.
terms.example: Trace whether the intended path is unbroken; use a continuity meter only on a de-energized circuit as demonstrated.

terms.definition: A circuit with a break that prevents sustained current through that path.
terms.example: Mark the break on the faulty paper diagram and explain which path it interrupts.

terms.definition: A specified location in a circuit where an observation or measurement is made.
terms.example: State which two locations an approved voltage measurement would compare.

terms.definition: Recorded observations, measurements, or results used to support a claim.
terms.example: Record what you actually observed before choosing the next diagnostic action.

terms.definition: A measure of opposition to current, expressed in ohms (Ω); for a resistor model, R = V ÷ I.
terms.example: At the supplied 6 V, changing the resistor model from 30 Ω to 60 Ω reduces predicted current from 0.20 A to 0.10 A.

name: MVP Job 29 · Budget electrical power and energy
description: Eight job words for budget electrical power and energy. Practice the meanings, then point to, sketch, calculate, or explain an example in your project. Knowledge target: Phase 5 job vocabulary. Practical skills are assessed in the job itself.

terms.definition: The rate at which energy is transferred or converted, measured in watts (W).
terms.example: A supplied 6-V load drawing 0.25 A converts energy at 6 × 0.25 = 1.5 W.

terms.definition: An amount transferred or converted by a system; electrical use may be counted in joules, watt-hours, or kilowatt-hours.
terms.example: Using the 1.5-W load for 2 h transfers 3 Wh of energy.

terms.definition: The unit of power, written W; one watt equals one joule per second.
terms.example: Label 1.5 W as power, not as the total energy used during the session.

terms.definition: The energy transferred by one watt operating for one hour; written Wh.
terms.example: Multiply watts by hours: 1.5 W × 2 h = 3 Wh.

terms.definition: An energy unit equal to 1,000 watt-hours, written kWh.
terms.example: Divide 3 Wh by 1,000 to obtain 0.003 kWh.

terms.definition: The duration for which a device is in use under the stated conditions.
terms.example: Reducing the hours used reduces the energy estimate when the power stays the same.

terms.definition: A stated price schedule; a classroom electricity calculation may use a fictional price per kWh.
terms.example: At the fictional $0.20/kWh rate, 0.003 kWh costs $0.0006 for energy alone.

terms.definition: A stated operating value or limit for a component, valid under specified conditions.
terms.example: Label the supplied voltage and current values as stated operating data rather than student measurements.

name: MVP Job 30 · Coordinate the system proposal
description: Eight job words for coordinate the system proposal. Practice the meanings, then point to, sketch, calculate, or explain an example in your project. Knowledge target: Phase 5 job vocabulary. Practical skills are assessed in the job itself.

terms.definition: A surrounding structure that contains or protects parts of a system.
terms.example: Build a paper base and four walls around the proposed low-voltage service route.

terms.definition: The space or opening needed to reach a part for operation, inspection, or maintenance.
terms.example: Demonstrate that the chosen opening lets a person reach the model component without tearing the enclosure.

terms.definition: The sum of the areas of the specified faces of a three-dimensional object.
terms.example: A 12 × 8 in base with four 4-in-high walls has 256 in² of area before tabs or cutting waste.

terms.definition: An itemized list of materials and components, including sizes and quantities needed for an assembly.
terms.example: List the enclosure pieces and the proposed circuit parts separately with quantities.

terms.definition: The space intentionally left between a part and another surface so the part can fit or move.
terms.example: Show the stated gaps between the enclosure walls and the service route.

terms.definition: Checking that related drawings, dimensions, components, and routes work together without conflict.
terms.example: Check that the route, removable opening, drawings, and material estimate describe the same design.

terms.definition: A trial version or model used to check a design before committing to a final product.
terms.example: Use the paper model to check fit and access before requesting hardware.

terms.definition: A written method that states what to test, the conditions, what to record, and how to judge the result.
terms.example: Name the access and fit checks, plus a future operating test if electrical hardware is unavailable.

name: MVP Job 31 · Write the improvement brief
description: Eight job words for write the improvement brief. Practice the meanings, then point to, sketch, calculate, or explain an example in your project. Knowledge target: Phase 6 job vocabulary. Practical skills are assessed in the job itself.

terms.definition: A short statement of the user, need, intended product, constraints, and success criteria for a project.
terms.example: Write the school user, observed problem, proposed product, constraints, and three checkable requirements.

terms.definition: A practical problem or requirement experienced by the person who will use the result.
terms.example: Describe the actual difficulty the school user experiences before suggesting a storage solution.

terms.definition: The work and deliverables included in a project, with its limits stated.
terms.example: State that this project delivers a proposal and model, with any installation requiring separate school arrangements.

terms.definition: A limit the design must satisfy, such as available space, materials, cost, or time.
terms.example: The supplied storage model has only 48 in of available width.

terms.definition: A measurable requirement or stated test used to decide whether the work meets the job's needs.
terms.example: Require the three model bins and their stated gaps to fit within the measured zone.

terms.definition: Whether a proposal can meet its requirements with the available space, resources, and methods.
terms.example: Check that three 14-in bins plus two 2-in gaps use 46 in of the available 48 in.

terms.definition: Information still needed before a claim or decision can be verified.
terms.example: List any unmeasured outside margins or user requirements that could change the layout.

terms.definition: A documented suggested solution with its supporting calculations, evidence, costs, and next steps.
terms.example: Support the suggested improvement with its brief, early dimension check, and planned next measurements.

name: MVP Job 32 · Survey for the proposal
description: Eight job words for survey for the proposal. Practice the meanings, then point to, sketch, calculate, or explain an example in your project. Knowledge target: Phase 6 job vocabulary. Practical skills are assessed in the job itself.

terms.definition: A recorded set of observations and measurements describing a site or work area.
terms.example: Record the proposal site's actual boundaries, features, sources, and checked dimensions.

terms.definition: A chosen reference point, line, or surface from which measurements are taken.
terms.example: Use one fixed corner or reference line to locate all critical features.

terms.definition: A point that marks the beginning or end of a measured distance.
terms.example: Make both surveyors measure between the same named faces before comparing their readings.

terms.definition: The smallest marked step a measuring tool can show; it does not guarantee the measurement is accurate.
terms.example: Record the tape's smallest marked increment alongside the critical fit measurements.

terms.definition: The size of the difference between two values without a positive or negative direction.
terms.example: Readings of 47 3/4 in and 47 7/8 in differ by 1/8 in.

terms.definition: A chain of labeled distances between successive features on a drawing.
terms.example: Check the sum of successive feature distances against one direct overall measurement.

terms.definition: A difference between values or records that are expected to agree.
terms.example: Investigate a disagreement in endpoints or alignment before specifying a tight fit.

terms.definition: Information still needed before a claim or decision can be verified.
terms.example: Mark an inaccessible dimension as unresolved rather than inventing a survey value.

name: MVP Job 33 · Design and calculate
description: Eight job words for design and calculate. Practice the meanings, then point to, sketch, calculate, or explain an example in your project. Knowledge target: Phase 6 job vocabulary. Practical skills are assessed in the job itself.

terms.definition: A drawing showing a space or object as viewed from directly above.
terms.example: Locate the bays, partitions, and outside boundaries in the top view.

terms.definition: A drawing looking straight at a vertical face, showing heights and vertical relationships.
terms.example: Show the same parts' heights in the side view and check that the views agree.

terms.definition: A dividing part between spaces whose thickness reduces the clear space available.
terms.example: Account for two 1/4-in-thick dividers inside the supplied 18-in clear opening.

terms.definition: The unobstructed distance available between the faces that bound a usable space.
terms.example: After subtracting 1/2 in of partitions, 17 1/2 in remains for the three clear bays.

terms.definition: An amount deliberately included for a stated purpose, such as overlap, cutting loss, or material thickness.
terms.example: Show each required gap or material thickness once in the dimension calculation.

terms.definition: A number that expresses parts of a whole; the denominator names the equal parts and the numerator counts them.
terms.example: Dividing 17 1/2 in among three bays gives 5 5/6 in per bay before choosing a practical layout method.

terms.definition: A limit the design must satisfy, such as available space, materials, cost, or time.
terms.example: A layout rounded independently in each bay must still fit the overall opening.

terms.definition: A quick estimate, comparison, or unit check used to see whether a calculated result makes sense.
terms.example: The bay width should be slightly less than 6 in because the partitions occupy some of the 18 in.

name: MVP Job 34 · Estimate and schedule the work
description: Eight job words for estimate and schedule the work. Practice the meanings, then point to, sketch, calculate, or explain an example in your project. Knowledge target: Phase 6 job vocabulary. Practical skills are assessed in the job itself.

terms.definition: A predicted cost broken into named items with quantities, unit prices, and subtotals.
terms.example: List every purchased material with size, quantity, unit price, and subtotal.

terms.definition: Material in the starting size available for making parts.
terms.example: Use the supplied 48-in lengths as the starting material for five 18-in strips.

terms.definition: The width of material removed by a cutting tool, which must be included when planning cuts.
terms.example: Include 1/8 in of cutting loss for each separating cut in the stock plan.

terms.definition: The count or measured amount of an item needed or purchased.
terms.example: A feasible plan requires three stock lengths because each supplies only two 18-in strips.

terms.definition: The price for one stated unit, such as one sheet or one foot of material.
terms.example: At the fictional $4 per stock length, three lengths cost $12 before other charges.

terms.definition: A stated allowance for identified uncertainty in a cost or time estimate.
terms.example: If you add an uncertainty allowance, state its reason and calculation separately from the material takeoff.

terms.definition: A task, material, or decision that must be ready before another activity can proceed.
terms.example: The cutting task depends on verified dimensions and available stock.

terms.definition: The planned order of steps in a job.
terms.example: Plan the order: verify, prepare, make, inspect, and revise.

name: MVP Job 35 · Prototype and inspect
description: Eight job words for prototype and inspect. Practice the meanings, then point to, sketch, calculate, or explain an example in your project. Knowledge target: Phase 6 job vocabulary. Practical skills are assessed in the job itself.

terms.definition: A trial version or model used to check a design before committing to a final product.
terms.example: Make a model or full-size layout to check the proposal's most important requirements.

terms.definition: A deliberate check of the work against its stated requirements.
terms.example: Compare the completed model with every acceptance criterion in the plan.

terms.definition: A measurable requirement or stated test used to decide whether the work meets the job's needs.
terms.example: The supplied fit requirement leaves 1/2 in clear at each end of a 24-in zone.

terms.definition: The space intentionally left between a part and another surface so the part can fit or move.
terms.example: Subtract both 1/2-in gaps to find a maximum outside model width of 23 in.

terms.definition: A distance between the outer faces of a part or assembly.
terms.example: Measure between the model's outer faces when checking its 23-in maximum width.

terms.definition: Recorded observations, measurements, or results used to support a claim.
terms.example: Record the measured fit and observed test result, including any test not yet performed.

terms.definition: An identified change to a drawing, plan, or product that replaces an earlier version.
terms.example: Update both the model and its drawing when a test leads to a change.

terms.definition: A new test after a change, using stated conditions so the results can be compared.
terms.example: Repeat the affected check after the revision and record the new result.

name: MVP Job 36 · Defend and hand over the proposal
description: Eight job words for defend and hand over the proposal. Practice the meanings, then point to, sketch, calculate, or explain an example in your project. Knowledge target: Phase 6 job vocabulary. Practical skills are assessed in the job itself.

terms.definition: The transfer of a completed work package and its essential information to the next person or user.
terms.example: Give the next person the brief, drawings, estimate, test record, revisions, and unresolved questions.

terms.definition: The ability to follow a result or decision back to its source measurement, calculation, drawing, or test.
terms.example: Show which site measurement and calculation support a dimension in the final drawing.

terms.definition: Recorded observations, measurements, or results used to support a claim.
terms.example: Support a design claim with a recorded inspection or test result from the project.

terms.definition: A boundary on what a method, model, or result can establish.
terms.example: Explain which real-system tests were not performed on the paper prototype.

terms.definition: A documented change to the agreed job requirements, including any effects on dimensions, cost, or time.
terms.example: Respond to a new requirement by identifying the drawings, calculations, and costs that need revision.

terms.definition: The increase divided by the original value, multiplied by 100%.
terms.example: A 15% increase on a fictional $80 estimate adds $12 and gives a revised total of $92.

terms.definition: An identified change to a drawing, plan, or product that replaces an earlier version.
terms.example: Check that every page in the handover package carries the current version.

terms.definition: A proposed next action supported by stated reasons and evidence.
terms.example: State the next action needed to move the proposal forward and explain what evidence supports it.
